title: Join grouped text
summary: GROUP_CONCAT joins text values from a group into one string.
introduction: GROUP_CONCAT joins text values from a group into one string. Your task: Change the separator to a slash.
learningObjectives: Change the separator to a slash.
Explain the example for join grouped text

blocks.text: GROUP_CONCAT joins text values from a group into one string. It can make a short list of names for a report.

Use MariaDB 10.11+ with its mariadb client in an empty practice database. These dialect-specific examples do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Keep the sample database separate from real records.

blocks.code:
WITH books AS (SELECT 'story' AS kind,'Moon Trip' AS title UNION ALL SELECT 'story','Tiny Seed')
SELECT kind,GROUP_CONCAT(title ORDER BY title SEPARATOR ', ') AS titles FROM books GROUP BY kind;
blocks.title: Join grouped text

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`GROUP BY` makes one summary group for each distinct combination of the named grouping values.
`GROUP_CONCAT` joins group text values with the chosen separator and ordering.

blocks.text: The story group has the text Moon Trip, Tiny Seed.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Large concatenated results can be limited by server settings. Do not use one long text list as a replacement for normal related rows.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change the separator to a slash.
